Software

◆ Built with AI
B1

FitFindr

◆ Python · Gradio · LLM agent

A shopping agent for secondhand clothes. You describe what you want in plain language — "a vintage graphic tee under $30 that works with baggy jeans" — and it searches listings, then styles the piece against the wardrobe you already own.

  • Three-step agent loop: search listings, build an outfit from the user's wardrobe, then write a shareable fit card.
  • Wardrobe stored against a JSON schema so suggestions reference real items, with an empty-wardrobe path for new users.
  • Guardrails on every step — a non-empty outfit suggestion is required before the fit card is generated, and failures return a readable error instead of a hallucination.
  • Filters on size and price so results stay inside what the user asked for.
PythonGradioTool callingJSON schemaPrompt design
B2

The Unofficial Guide

◆ RAG · ChromaDB · Groq

Ask about a professor and get an answer built only from real student reviews. Every response lists the exact review chunks behind it, so you can check the source instead of trusting the model.

  • End-to-end retrieval pipeline: ingest, clean, and chunk 10 RateMyProfessors sources into 47 embedded chunks in a ChromaDB vector store.
  • Embeddings via all-MiniLM-L6-v2, with a top-k slider so you can widen or tighten retrieval per question.
  • Off-topic questions are refused before any LLM call — cheaper, and it can't invent an answer it has no sources for.
  • Answers cite documents inline and can be scoped to a single professor.
PythonChromaDBGroqGradioEmbeddings
B3

University Course Management System

Python · Data structures

A full course-registration system built from scratch on my own data structures — student records, course catalogs, prerequisite chains, and waitlists, with no library shortcuts.

  • Hash map with separate chaining and dynamic rehashing to hold lookups at O(1) as the catalog grows.
  • Recursive binary search for retrieval; merge sort and quick sort for roster ordering at O(n log n).
  • Enrollment validates prerequisites before registering a student and routes over-capacity courses through a custom linked queue.
  • Object-oriented throughout, so students, courses, and rosters each own their own rules.
PythonOOPHash mapsSortingADTs
Catalog    ── HashMap<code, Course>
              └─ separate chaining + rehash ...... O(1)

Lookup     ── recursive binary search ......... O(log n)

Roster     ── merge sort / quick sort ......... O(n log n)

Enrollment ── prerequisite check
              └─ over capacity → LinkedQueue ADT
